item.title: Mass Effect fans have taken their mission to save BioWare and its beloved sci-fi franchise to EA headquarters with a truck displaying the #SaveMassEffect message.
item.description:
Mass Effect fans have taken their mission to save BioWare and its beloved sci-fi franchise to EA headquarters with a truck displaying the #SaveMassEffect message.
The latest update to what has ballooned into a full-blown movement arrived today when the dedicated group of fans known as We are Mass Effect announced they had brought their latest billboard right to the publisher's front door. Where their last push arrived in the form of a daylong billboard in New York City's Times Square, this mobile effort will see a truck sharing the word on the streets surrounding EA and EA Sports HQ in Redwood City, California.
Anyone who visits the area today can spot the truck, which features signage updated with a handy QR code and website URL directing curious players to SaveMassEffect.com. The goal, as We are Mass Effect's Mer told IGN, is to "spread the word and bring as much attention to the movement as possible, " but putting it in EA's front lawn after the publisher put Mass Effect games on hold and shuttered BioWare also sends a message of its own.
🚨 WE ARE BACK ON THE STREETSTogether with @kalaelizabeth, our first mobile billboard is now outside EA's HQ and EA Sports HQ. 📸 If you're nearby, send us pictures! Please don't enter EA's property.#SaveMassEffect https://t.co/5N87nz8uDR
"Social media can sometimes make devastating events feel distant or abstract," We are Mass Effect told IGN when asked about the truck. "It’s easy to read about these news online without fully grasping the human impact behind it. So we wanted to bring the movement into the physical world and make that support visible. We want to remind people that real people have been impacted by the closure of BioWare and the cancellation of the game. We wanted to show them that there is a community that deeply cares about the legacy they’ve created. For us this has never been just about the IP but the people behind it and their work."
Driving a truck around EA HQ will certainly gather some attention, but detractors have warned that no amount of momentum will get the publisher to budge. The goal, as We are Mass Effect has outlined, is not only to offer a message of unity for those who love BioWare franchises like Mass Effect or Dragon Age, but to raise awareness about the human beings affected by these changes, too.
Another mobile billboard will appear near BioWare's former offices tomorrow, with the final billboard launching during The Game Awards next month. Billboard organizer, fundraiser, and content creator Kala Elizabeth told IGN the plan is to drive it around the TGA ceremony for around four hours.
"For me, after our billboards are up, I plan to support the devs however possible and bring visibility to anything else that we can support, but as of right now, I don't have any plans to crowdfund more billboards because these were already exhausting," Elizabeth added with a laugh.
Our first #SaveMassEffect mobile billboard is outside of EA HQ and EA Sports HQ in Redwood! Go get a picture! (do not go into EA if you do) https://t.co/1L3vTqTojP
Meanwhile, We are Mass Effect said it is currently putting the finishing touches on a video featuring Mass Effect fans, actors, and contributors for N7 Day tomorrow, November 7. Included in the lineup are Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer. The group is also pushing N7 Play Day in an attempt to boost Steam player numbers for Mass Effect: Legendary Edition.
"And, as a fun throwback to 2012, we’re planning to send cupcakes decorated in N7 colors to EA’s headquarters in Redwood City next week," the group said. "There’s a lot happening, and we don’t plan on stopping anytime soon. The response from the community has shown us just how much Mass Effect and BioWare’s legacy mean to people, and we want to continue finding creative ways to make that support visible."
EA closed down BioWare weeks ago, but as fans get ready for N7 Day, they've done anything but go gently into the night. In addition to that Times Square billboard, a petition urging EA to allow the franchise to live in some capacity has gained more than 300,000 signatures. Save Mass Effect graffiti was also reportedly spray-painted outside of an EA office building in Madrid, while another was decorated with tombstones featuring shuttered studios.
"People are upset, not only about what happened to BioWare, but about the many studios, IPs, and talented devs that have gone through the same thing," We are Mass Effect added. "What we can do is to encourage them to keep supporting the initiatives that the community are organizing, and to keep showing up. We don't want this to become another story, another beloved IP that is forgotten. The most important thing is to make sure people continue paying attention and understand just how much these games and the devs behind them mean to so many."
Mass Effect N7 Wearable LED Helmet Images
"I think the most important thing is supporting the devs and showing that we care," Elizabeth said. "N7 Day is a huge day for Mass Effect and this year is very different. It's important that we're loud and show our support. Signing the petition, using the hashtag, and amplifying the voices of the devs."
A new documentary that filmed the studio's final years was announced just yesterday. While fans hope to make a difference at EA's front door, the publisher is still pushing merchandise for the paused franchise for N7 Day. Meanwhile, a Canadian politician has recently joined the fight.
Image courtesy of @kalaelizabeth on X/Twitter.

item.title: The father of late Pokémon influencer Avery the Poké Kid is asking The Pokémon Company to create a special card in honor of his son.
item.description:
The father of late Pokémon influencer Avery the Poké Kid is asking The Pokémon Company to create a special card in honor of his son.
Avery the Poké Kid was a prominent and cheerful voice in the Pokémon Trading Card Game community. He died in September 2026 at 12 years old in after a seven-year-battle with pancreatic cancer; he went viral posthumously when his family shared a video of his final card pack opening a few days after his death, in which he excitedly pulled a 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR card.
Now, his father is putting forth a public request to The Pokémon Company to make a special card in Avery’s honor.
On November 6, Christian Garcia — Avery’s father — published a tearful video on Instagram with a special plea to "immortalize" his son in the hobby he loved the most.
“Trying to figure out how to carry on Avery’s legacy has been the biggest challenge of the last couple months,” Garcia said. “…I want to make a plea to anyone, literally anyone from The Pokémon Company: If you’re watching this video, I want to figure out how to immortalize him somehow in the trading card game he loved so much.
“That kid literally was the embodiment of a Pokémon Master, and we’re hopeful, and I think it would be the coolest thing to open up a pack of cards and chase our son. If someone at The Pokémon Company is watching, please get a hold of us.”
Pokemon Happy Meal Cards 2026
Fans and fellow collectors are doing everything they can to get the attention of The Pokémon Company, with most agreeing that it would only make sense to make his card some iteration of a Jirachi, given his viral pull that took over social media after his death.
Avery’s heartbreaking Jirachi pull even caught the attention of the card’s artist, who posted an emotional reaction to the news on her Twitter/X account. “I’m so deeply moved. I’m so glad I kept drawing. I’ve honestly been in tears ever since I saw this,” she wrote. “‘I want my art to bring happiness to people.’ That’s one of the reasons I draw. I’m so glad I put that wish into this piece.”
This latest statement from Avery’s father follows a September announcement from the influencer’s family in response to scalpers inflating the price of the 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR card as a result of his viral video.
“We are not involved in or benefiting from any cards being sold in Avery’s name or likeness. We have not approved these sales. We have asked sellers to take their listings down. Please do so immediately. This does not honor Avery’s generous heart. We are mourning our son and caring for our children. Please let us do that in peace,” they wrote at the time.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: IGN got the chance to catch up with Nicolas Cage on the red carpet for his upcoming sports comedy flick Madden, where he opened up about his thoughts on Spider-Noir’s cancellation.
item.description:
IGN got the chance to catch up with Nicolas Cage on the red carpet for his upcoming sports comedy flick Madden, where he opened up about his thoughts on Spider-Noir’s cancellation.
Released on Prime Video earlier this year, Cage stars as Ben Reilly in this animated take on New York’s resident web-slinger. Available to watch in both black and white and color, the show received strong reviews on the outset, but officially got canned by the streamer in September after falling out of its top 10 shows — oddly, much to Cage’s relief.
In a statement to Deadline, Cage said, “For me, one season is perfect, having said what I wanted to say with this dangerous, innovative, pop-art Spider-Man. Onwards, upwards, inwards.”
Spider-Noir #1 Exclusive Preview Gallery
He doubled down on this sentiment while chatting with IGN’s Jeffrey Vega in early November, who asked if the actor felt there was still more of Ben Reilly’s story left to tell.
“No,” Cage answered. “I meant it when I said what I said. It’s a perfect season. You never wanna get stuck repeating a character and wear out your welcome. Ben Riley is so idiosyncratic. I was doing something that was pretty high-risk, tightrope stuff — if you do that for season 2, season 3, you could really wear out your welcome.
“So when they didn’t pick it up, I was like, 'Whew, thank you!' Because now I’m doing True Detective, and that’s only one season. It’s better that way, you know? I liked it when you would see Rock Hudson and Macmillan ? and it’s one season. I didn’t wanna keep repeating it. I don’t like repeating myself. It’s perfect, and I love that character. I love that season, and it will always be there and always be fresh.”
Aside from not wanting to rehash his character’s story, Cage wouldn’t return to the Spider-Noir series anyway, as he famously parted ways with Amazon over its stance on AI. In a blistering statement, he revealed that he refused to sign a waiver to use artificial intelligence on the animated series and confirmed that he was unlikely to ever work with the company again.
"Amazon is a very AI-friendly company, to the tune of $50 billion invested in OpenAI. I'm not an AI-friendly actor," Cage said. "I'm not part of their club. I didn't sign the waiver to use AI on Spider-Noir. I'll probably not work with that studio again, but that's OK."
Cage has been open about his distaste for AI, saying at the 2025 Saturn Awards that "Robots cannot reflect the human condition for us. That is a dead end if an actor lets one AI robot manipulate his or her performance even a little bit, an inch will eventually become a mile and all integrity, purity, and truth of art will be replaced by financial interests only. We can’t let that happen."
Cage is currently gearing up for the November 18 release of Madden, wherein he portrays the titular John Madden – a performance that has already been a source of viral debate among fans.

item.title: Ed Boon is stirring up excitement in the fighting game community after releasing a poll asking fans what they’d like the next Mortal Kombat installment to be called.
item.description:
Ed Boon is stirring up excitement in the fighting game community after releasing a poll asking fans what they’d like the next Mortal Kombat installment to be called.
It’s been a rough time for Mortal Kombat fans. The series’ latest game, MK1, officially stopped receiving new content updates in May 2025, and its presence at competitive tournaments has been lackluster, at best.
Players are eager for more news on the next game in the franchise, which co-creator Ed Boon confirmed was officially in the works in May 2026. It’s been pretty quiet since then — but now, it appears that Boon is testing the waters to see what fans are expecting.
Mortal Kombat Flawless Victory: A Visual History of the Iconic Series Excerpt
On November 6, 2026, Boon published two polls on X/Twitter. The first asked, “What would you want the next Mortal Kombat to be called?” giving options for Mortal Kombat 13, Mortal Kombat 12, and Mortal Kombat 2. (Thus far, 43% of participants have voted for Mortal Kombat 2, with 33% choosing 13 and 23% choosing 12.)
His second poll is far more intriguing, asking: “With two great Marvel fighting games being made by different teams, which would you like to see come out next? Marvel Tokon 2 by Arc System Works, or Marvel vs Capcom 4?” (Unsurprisingly, the overwhelming majority of fans chose MvC4.)
With 2 great Marvel fighting games being made by different teams. Which would you like to see come out next?Marvel Tokkon 2 by Arc System works.orMarvel vs Capcom 4
This is an interesting query coming from the developer of the Injustice series, and an odd one, given that the likelihood of another Marvel vs Capcom game happening anytime soon — if ever — seems extremely improbable. The FGC has already tied itself in knots about Tokon’s player count and difficult PC launch, while, mechanically, there’s a significant divide as to whether or not it’s actually fun at a competitive level. On the other hand, the MvC series appeared to die a slow, painful death with Infinite, though it has received a second wind over the last few years (in no small part thanks to the Beyond fan mod).
This question follows oodles of rumors regarding the next Injustice game, which has been all but outright confirmed by Boon. Fans have already uncovered resumes from stunt performers that list Injustice 3, and rumors that playtests were underway for the game surfaced earlier this year.
Boon reacted to the rumors back in September in response to a tweet claiming that NetherRealm was testing Injustice 3, Mortal Kombat 13, and / or Mortal Kombat 9. “All false,” he wrote. “Appreciate the interest & enthusiasm, but just because a game isn’t currently being tested externally doesn’t necessarily mean the game isn’t in development.”
For now, we’ll just have to wait and see what Boon and NetherRealm have in store for their next game. In the meantime, you can read our interview with the cast of the Street Fighter movie, who said they’re more than willing to take part in a crossover film with the cast of the Mortal Kombat franchise. Boon even responded to our report, saying that he’d rather have a Street Fighter x Mortal Kombat game before a movie gets made.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Germany has a unique legal loophole that lets 60 employees take time off work to play GTA 6 without putting their jobs in jeopardy.
item.description:
Germany has a unique legal loophole that lets 60 employees take time off work to play GTA 6 without putting their jobs in jeopardy.
GTA 6 is shaping up to be one of the biggest pop culture moments in history, and perhaps the biggest video game launch of all time. With this in mind, it’s no surprise that oodles of gamers are planning to call out of work to play it, with estimates showing a 17% increase in time-off requests for its launch date on November 19.
This trend isn’t limited to the US, either, as a fair amount of fans across the globe will also be staying home to play. Luckily, fans in Germany literally have legal protections that will allow them to do this without putting their jobs on the line.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
Bildungsurlaub, Germany's legally mandated paid learning leave for certified training courses, is offering a state-funded educational course on storytelling in video games that would give gamers three days off to play GTA 6 from November 18 - 20. Titled ‘Open World Games: Lessons from a Digital World,’ this program is open to 60 participants, letting them use this paid leave to “explore storytelling, digital culture, and collaboration through open-world gaming,” as explained in a press release shared with IGN.
Students will gather in guided groups to complete assignments in the game and use their observations to learn “practical lessons on storytelling, motivation, community-building, and collaboration.” One of these lessons explores how Easter eggs create engagement with players, examining how brands, learning programs, and teams can “borrow from that dynamic.”
“Modern learning should meet people where their curiosity already lives. Open worlds are built on stories, choices, communities, and constant problem-solving. That makes them powerful places to learn,” says Carlo Dreschel, founder of course provider Dein Bildungsurlaub. “Like many other educational providers, we've incorporated elements of gaming, such as role-playing, simulations, game mechanics and reward systems, into learning experiences before. But with ‘Open World Games,’ we're taking that approach to an entirely new level.”
23-year-old accountant Victoria is one of the students who’s signed up for this course. Hailing from Berlin, she’s an “avid gamer” who says she’s curious about how this program will aid her professional life.
“I am curious to see what I can really learn from the experience. My usual day to day is driven by routine. I believe the course will break this routine and offer a new perspective to the same old problems. Maybe the experience of pulling off a high speed car chase can help me handle stressful clients in the future,” she said in a statement.
Participants must be 18 years of age or older and have access to a suitable device and a licensed open-world game in order to take part in this course. It will take place over a three-day period online, with an additional in-person event planned in Berlin.

item.title: Sony Santa Monica Studios' God of War Ragnarok tops the list of highest-grossing PlayStation Studios games of the PS5 generation, according to Alinea Analytics.
item.description:
Sony Santa Monica Studios' God of War Ragnarok tops the list of highest-grossing PlayStation Studios games of the PS5 generation, according to Alinea Analytics.
The game data company's head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, shared information related to sales for titles published under the PlayStation banner in a Substack post today. It features a list of 10 games estimated to have emerged as Sony's best performers so far.
You can probably guess at least some of the games that managed to crack the top 10 list, but there are a few interesting inclusions in there, too. God of War Ragnarok, for example, is placed at number one with an estimated $1.4 billion in gross revenue. Spider-Man 2 is second at $1.3 billion, with Gran Turismo 7 placed third at $841.9 million. You can see the full list below.
Here's the 10 top-grossing PlayStation Studios games of this generation (@alineaanalytics estimates). Together, the 10 games generated over $6.5 billion across PlayStation (84.7%), Steam (14.1%), and Xbox (1.2% via just Helldivers 2).Full write-up over on Substack. https://t.co/3XLgJdTqUM
PlayStation Studios' Top 10 Highest-Grossing PS5 Games, According to Alinea Analytics
1. God of War Ragnarok – $1.4 billion
2. Spider-Man 2 – $1.3 billion
3. Gran Turismo 7 – $841.9 million
4. Helldivers 2 – $786.3 million
5. Horizon Forbidden West – $485.8 million
6. Ghost of Yōtei – $410.1 million
7. The Last of Us Part 1 – $341.3 million
8. Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart – $334.9 million
9. Stellar Blade – $316.9 million
10. Astro Bot – $292.6 million
These 10 games alone have generated $6.5 billion for PlayStation. Although the list only includes titles from the PS5 generation, the numbers here do account for other platforms. Astro Bot, for example, is exclusive to PS5 and earned its amount only through the estimated 4.7 million copies it sold on that platform.
God of War Ragnarok, meanwhile, is also available on PS4 and PC, with Alinea Analytics' breakdown showing its revenue accumulated via 21.6 million copies across all three platforms. Of its performance on PlayStation, 75.2% of its 20.1 million share of copies sold were on PS5, specifically, with 27.5% of all sales on PS4 and PS5 being physical. Elliott called the Norse God of War sequel an evergreen title for Sony, explaining that in 2026 alone it's managed to sell 1.1 million copies. That's an impressive feat compared even to brand-new games from this year, and it's only more impressive when you consider that it was made accessible to PlayStation Extra subscribers nearly two years ago in January of 2025. Alinea Analytics estimates show that 6.7 million PlayStation Plus users have accessed it via the service.
PS5 Digital Console 30th Anniversary Limited Edition
Ghost of Yōtei may have technically been trailing behind its predecessor as of October, but at least for now, its recent Echoes of Sekigahara expansion has helped it land in sixth. As of today's update, it's said to have sold 5.5 million copies as a PS5 exclusive. Another interesting addition from the list is Stellar Blade, which is technically a second-party release published by PlayStation Studios. Today's data accounts for sales across PS5 and Steam (a Nintendo Switch 2 version launched yesterday) and shows that 59.7% of its revenue was earned from the former and 40.3% from the latter.
Alinea Analytics' breakdown is not an official look into where sales are at with Sony's gaming division. Meanwhile, its update follows official information released by the PlayStation company just earlier this week. It came with the news that it had raised its sales forecast while also sharing figures for Marvel's Wolverine for the first time. For more, you can see how PlayStation's Bloodborne has held up in the 11 years since its launch on PS4.

item.title: A Canadian politician has started an official government petition to save Mass Effect developer BioWare.
item.description:
Update: Canadian MP Don Davies has provided comment on the BioWare petition:
“BioWare has cultivated an international following from their renowned video game franchises like Mass Effect, Baldur’s Gate, and Dragon Age. Canada’s video game industry creates some of our most important cultural exports, and BioWare was among our biggest success stories.
Electronic Arts, their American parent company, was never invested in the success of BioWare since they purchased the studio as part of a larger acquisition in 2007. This is a pattern with video game publishers like EA. They buy smaller developers, set unrealistic timelines, overwork their employees, and meddle in the development process, resulting in poorer quality games. Then, when sales fail to meet expectations, they blame the developers, lay off workers, and eventually shut down the studio for short-term profit.
New Democrats want BioWare to stay in business, preferably under Canadian control. We believe that the employees at BioWare ought to have the first opportunity to buy back their studio and continue making the games that fans love. The petition primarily asks the federal government to provide the required capital. This is absolutely possible. Our goal with the petition is to demonstrate just how many Canadians believe this is a worthwhile investment in our entertainment industry.”
Original story continues below.
It's already been a couple of weeks since EA shut down BioWare, but the fight to save the studio is still picking up steam. And now, after a fanmade petition reached 300,000 signatures, a Canadian politician has started an official government petition to save the Mass Effect developer.
Petition e-7898 was initiated by Burnaby, British Columbia resident Brendan Routh, and sponsored by Vancouver Kingsway MP Don Davies. The petition primarily calls upon the Canadian government to provide BioWare with the necessary capital to secure independence and ownership of its intellectual property. However, it further asks the government to protect Canadian businesses from "being dictated by American and foreign corporate interests."
The petition also asks the government to "champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights at the centre of Canada's national identity by preserving BioWare's invaluable contribution to the global entertainment industry."
Every IGN Mass Effect Review
At the time of writing, the petition has already racked up 2,861 signatures. And while that's a far cry from the 307,000 signatures on the change.org petition, the Canadian government only requires that 500 people sign it before it's brought before the House of Commons for discussion. And while it will be presented to the House of Commons, it remains to be seen whether or not the Canadian government will actually act on it.
However, Don Davies has taken to Bluesky to argue the petition's merits. In a post, Davies argues "BioWare’s US parent company, EA, has decided to close the studio. These publishers buy developers, run them into the ground, and rip them apart for profit. There's a pattern of US companies buying Canadian businesses and shutting them down, costing Canadians their jobs."
In a followup post, Davies continues: "The developers at BioWare know how to run their studio. They know how to make the games that fans love. They should be given the first opportunity – and the federal support – to buy it and run it themselves."
This petition comes a little over a week after another Canadian politician, Avi Lewis, spoke out about the closure, and floated the idea of the Canadian government helping BioWare gain its independence from EA. But, now that there's a petition that has crossed its signature threshold, there's actually a slim possibility that something is going to happen.
I've reached out to Don Davies for comment, and I'll update this article if I hear anything. But, who knows; maybe there's a chance that something will come of that incredible leaked Mass Effect 5 trailer, after all.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: World of Warcraft Forever came out earlier this week, and has been a massively successful launch. It almost begs the question, "Why wait this long?" Well, Blizzard has revealed what made it finally release the Classic+ game mode.
item.description:
World of Warcraft Forever came out earlier this week, and has been a massively successful launch. It almost begs the question, "Why wait this long?" Well, Blizzard has revealed what made it finally release the Classic+ game mode.
In an interview with Bloomberg, Blizzard senior game designer Josh Greenfield revealed that the developer had been kicking around the idea of WoW Forever since before Classic released in 2019, but the team ultimately pulled the trigger on the straight-up port of Vanilla WoW first. But while Forever was put on the backburner, the Classic team started to get a little bit more experimental as the old-school version of the MMO aged.
Then, in 2023, Blizzard released a new game mode, Season of Discovery, which took Classic and made some pretty radical changes, like ability gems and turning old 5-player dungeons like Blackfathom Deeps into full-scale raids. This game mode had some pretty immediate impacts on even retail WoW, like when Blizzard released Mists of Pandaria Remix in 2024 and Legion Remix in 2025.
World of Warcraft: Forever Screenshots
But it turns out that the biggest impact that Season of Discovery had was making the WoW team pull the trigger on Classic+, or Forever. According to Greenfield, the community response to Season of Discovery is what made Forever actually happen. He told Bloomberg, “That’s really when the conversation started around, ‘Hey, what does a permanent version of this game look like?’”
Season of Discovery's success also helped convince leadership to allow development on Forever to proceed, and once the team started getting the new graphics engines in place, everything seems to come together. According to that Bloomberg piece, Northshire Abbey became a tech demo of sorts, and one that won over pretty much everyone at Blizzard.
And it's good that it did. IGN's early review of World of Warcraft Forever is extremely positive, and while it'll obviously be a while before the full review is finished, reviewer Len Hafer says, "[Blizzard] made me believe I can go home again – and that home is somewhere I want to spend more time, with new surprises to discover. Let's see if they can keep it up for 47 more levels. Watch this space for updates in the weeks to come."
Players seem impressed with WoW Forever as well, especially on the back of an extremely smooth launch that was almost completely free of any kind of server problems. It doesn't hurt that Blizzard dedicated a ton of hardware to keeping the servers running smoothly at launch, with around 200TB of memory.
World of Warcraft Forever or Retail?

Back in August, when preorders went up for the translucent green Xbox Series X | X25 Special Edition console, they sold out almost instantly. That was a bummer for longtime Xbox fans who wanted to get their hands on one of these limited-edition 25th-anniversary consoles. Now you have another chance, thanks to Amazon. Instead of doing preorders on a first-come-first-served basis, Amazon is letting anyone interested request an invite to buy this special-edition Xbox (you can request one here).
Xbox Series X - X25 Limited Edition Invite Request
Requesting an invite doesn’t mean you’ll necessarily end up being invited to buy a console. But it gives you a chance to be invited, which is better than nothing. As Amazon says, “If invited to purchase, you’ll get an email when the item is available. Not all requests will be granted.”
The console is meant to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Xbox. It’s set to release on November 13 and costs (the curiously specific price) $909.23. Only 25,000 numbered consoles are being manufactured, which explains the difficulty people have had securing a preorder.
So what do you get if you do end up buying it? You get a 1TB Xbox Series X console, decked out in translucent green. The front of the console has an X25 logo, and when you turn it on, the X logo glows green as well. You also get a matching controller (which is also sold separately, and is still available at some retailers). Finally, you get a digital copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved, a remake of the campaign from the original Halo (see our review).
XBOX Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition (Available Now)
Overall, this has been an extremely popular item among IGN readers. It’s a great-looking piece of hardware that celebrates 25 years since the original Xbox hit store shelves. If you want one, or even if you might be interested in one, there’s no reason not to request an invite.
Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games, LEGO sets, and 4K Blu-rays. You can follow him on Bluesky.

item.title: Ex-Call of Duty creative strategist Robert Bowling and comedian Dane Cook have revealed a brand new genre-bending video game known as Vicious Vocab, exclusively to IGN.
item.description:
Ex-Call of Duty creative strategist Robert Bowling and comedian Dane Cook have revealed a brand new, genre-bending video game known as Vicious Vocab, exclusively to IGN.
Vicious Vocab is a genre-bending spin on casual word games like Scrabble, Words With Friends, and Wordle, with a big twist. While Bowling and Cook are careful not to share much about the twist to preserve some surprises, the game goes well beyond mixing and matching letters to make new words. The words have power and meaning… and they can dramatically change not only what happens to you, but the entire genre of game that you’re playing.
Check out the trailer below to get an idea of the unexpected shift that happens in Vicious Vocab.
Made by a team of five people who collectively call themselves “funcool games,” Vicious Vocab is described as “Scrabble meets Balatro in a backroom casino.” On its own, it’s a fun twist on the word game genre. There’s an action element, which has led the team to referring to the game as a “word brawler” or, in Cook’s words, a first-person speller.
You can “take damage” based on certain words. You can then counter it with another word, so long as you have the right letters. For instance, as seen in the trailer, if you spell out “torch” or “fire,” you might take fire damage. You can then spell out “water” or “ice” and extinguish the flame to stop yourself from taking more damage. These effects add interesting layers to the expected mechanics of a word game.
“That's something you don't get in normal word games,” said Bowling when speaking with IGN. “Building systems that work against systems that work against other systems. When you're four layers deep in a combo, that is the stuff that really makes you feel like, 'Am I playing a word game anymore?' I know I'm making words, I know I'm using letters, but the sort of chaining of events you can get yourself into really sort of that's when you start breaking out of one genre and start making something new.”
However, as the trailer reveals, Vicious Vocab can shift in an incredibly unexpected direction, taking it from a cozy game your mom might play casually on the couch to something in line with The Stanley Parable. If you play the right words, you can move away from the word board and have an entirely new experience that you would've never anticipated.
"We both want to create holy s**t moments," said Cook. "We want to create memorable moments."
Although there are plans to add multiplayer to the game at some point, it is a single-player narrative driven game. If you want to, you can just stick to the more traditional word game and play that “infinitely,” but the game also expands in a whole other direction beyond that.
“We're building out a very deep single player experience that has over 20 different narrative endings, lots of achievements, but the plan is to also expand into a multiplayer experience,” said Bowling. “So there is going to be both. They go in very different directions though, where the multiplayer experience is all about replayability and the single player experience is all about a lot of endings, still a lot of replayability. You can still play it infinitely, but there's a lot more narrative to it that may or may not be in the multiplayer side of it. Think about it as a stem that breaks off into two directions and they get equally weird, but in different ways.”
The pairing of an ex-Call of Duty developer and a comedian is one that may seem unlikely, but it actually dates back 20 years. The two met when Bowling was starting out as a community manager at Infinity Ward and somehow, this led to them playing Call of Duty 2 together. During a match of Capture the Flag, Bowling was impressed that Cook was actually a valuable asset who played the objective instead of mindlessly running around trying to farm kills. From there, a friendship was formed, which eventually led to Cook lending his voice to the “battle chatter” (voice lines for characters yelling out commands and call outs in-game) in the Modern Warfare games.
The Best Call of Duty Multiplayer Games
Over the years, Cook would drum up cool ideas for a game to pitch to Bowling, but it wasn’t until about a year ago when one of those seeds actually began to materialize into a full-fledged game. The initial idea was simple: a word game where your words have an effect. If you write "bomb," it might blow up the other words on the board. It was cute and novel, but as the small team began to brainstorm ideas for effects, it eventually took them into new unexpected directions, such as moving away from the word board.
If this were any other game, developers might say this is a bad idea, because it can lead to a spiral of new mechanics and concepts, but funcool games felt that this exploration that knocks down boundaries and defined genre identities was exciting and worth pursuing.
“It's like, ‘No, I want the game to be wherever it takes us and then see how far can we go,’" said Bowling. “Because you do have some natural constraints from a design standpoint. It's not [like you can] literally do anything because this is all bespoke, handcrafted stuff. So then the question became like, ‘Oh my God, how far can you go with just seven letters and your vocabulary?’ That became the sort of development mantra of, ‘Where is the end?’ And I'll be honest with you, we haven't found it yet. You can get yourself in a lot of weird scenarios with just seven letters, and that has been the most fun. Honestly, when we first started talking about this idea, I loved it as a nugget of the ideal, enough to be like, ‘All right, let's dig into it.’ But I didn't yet know how deep you could go with it.
“Once I cracked that nut creatively, I was like, ‘I love this. I need to play this and I want it to get extremely weird. Dane has a better vocabulary than me. I always go back to weird. I think Stanley Parable. I think give me something where I'm like, ‘What the hell is happening?’"
For Cook, this is sort of a culmination of his career. When he was a kid, his dad would read the dictionary to have a better vocabulary for his job, as he was a color commentator for local hockey games. Cook thought this was “lame” when he was young, but grew to have a better understanding of that process once he became a comic. His entire job as a stand up comic is about using carefully calculated vocabulary to have the best effect on the audience.
“I later found myself saying to him, ‘I paint verbal pictures, and if I repeat the same word over and over, it's blurring the audible version, the audio version, and yet if I have different vernacular for ways to describe something, you're always giving it musicality,’” said Cook. “So lo and behold, I used to have screensavers, word of the day, and things that I could then implement into my standup that I thought helped the musicality paint the verbal pictures.
“I love language, and it's something that to this day when you come down and see me do a show, you'll go, ‘Oh wait, I saw that you used ‘malleable’ to describe blah, blah, blah, blah." I say, "Yeah, because I think it danced better than just saying ‘bent.’ So, [words are] very much a part of my identity and how I like to impact. And again, as a fan of games like this, growing up, playing Scrabble, these are the games that I've always appreciated and enjoyed. So, to feel like I might be able to take it to a new place that also maybe even expands on what those games have been, I hope we pull it off, because I'm really excited at the possibilities.”
In addition to Vicious Vocab, Robert Bowling is also working on a new, larger-scale FPS game from a new studio known as //18.bravo. The game will feature a single-player story and a PvP multiplayer mode, but the game is actively pushing back on live-service trends. Dane Cook also has a new documentary titled Funny Money available on Netflix today.
Vicious Vocab will release on PC at an undisclosed date in the not-too-distant future. No pricing plan has been decided yet.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: ENDIX, the fully digital, free-to-attend gaming expo, is now live from today, November 6, through November 8, and it offers guests from around the world the opportunity to step onto a virtual show floor to check out over 50 games, play demos, watch world premieres and exclusive trailers, and even speak to the studios and publishers behind the titles through integrated voice chat, all from the comfort of their own homes.
item.description:
ENDIX, the fully digital, free-to-attend gaming expo, is now live from today, November 6, through November 8, and it offers guests from around the world the opportunity to step onto a virtual show floor to check out over 50 games, play demos, watch world premieres and exclusive trailers, and even speak to the studios and publishers behind the titles through integrated voice chat, all from the comfort of their own homes.
By downloading ENDIX for free on Steam or the Epic Games Store, guests can create their own avatar and walk through the show floor, stopping at virtual themed halls, rooftop spaces, and dedicated publisher areas, including THQ Nordic Island, where players can check out Titan Quest II, Expeditions: Samurai, Fatekeeper, and The Eternal Life of Goldman.
ENDIX Expo November 2026 Images and Screenshots
Bohemia Interactive has its own dedicated area featuring Silica and Nailcrown, 505 Games is there with Among the Trolls, Frozen District is showing off House Flipper 2: Pets, Forgery Craft, and Dreampainters, Noodlecake Games has Tiebreakers, Monkey Brain, and Harpooner on display, Playism features Homura Hime, and Horrified Triangles will offer guests a chance to experience Haunted Bloodlines and Alpha Nomos.
These are only a few of the games currently on display, and there will be even more to explore in ENDIX. For example. Alienware and Elgato are the brand partners this year and will have mini-games for guests to enjoy and a unique activation, respectively. Furthermore, guests can head over to the City Mega Stand to see Crema's Temtem: Pioneers, walk over to the laid-back Cozy Area, or test their mettle within the eerie halls of the horror-themed Theatrum Obscurum.
“Every edition of ENDIX starts with the same question: how do we make the most unique and inclusive event experience for gamers from all over the world?” said Nikos Perifanis, founder of ENDIX. “Seeing publishers like THQ Nordic, 505 Games, Frozen District, Noodlecake, and Playism build their spaces inside ENDIX, right alongside dozens of independent studios, tells us we’re on the right track. Whether you’re a two-person studio, solo dev or a publisher with decades of history, everyone shares the same virtual space, and every player can walk right up to any and connect. We can’t wait to open the virtual doors in November.”
For more, check out ENDIX's website to learn all about this playable gaming event you can check out right now, assuming you are reading this between November 6-8! Additionally, you can see many of the excluisve trailers on IGN.com and IGN's YouTube channel.

Wounds are still fresh coming into this year’s N7 Day, a day traditionally dedicated to celebrating Mass Effect’s history and announcing updates about its future. The festivities are now shrouded by the news of Bioware’s closure and the worst possible update for any franchise: the cancellation of Mass Effect 5.
Given how recently EA announced the studio shakeup, it stands to reason that Bioware had already prepared at least something for the N7 Day festivities. Some of these plans are still coming to fruition. Namely, a merch drop, including a new and improved version of the wearable N7 LED helmet.
Mass Effect N7 Wearable LED Helmet Images
The new helmet is a wearable replica of Shepard’s helmet from Mass Effect 3. It’s essentially an 'upgraded' version of the N7 replica helmet that launched alongside Mass Effect Legendary Edition back in 2020, adding a layer of padding as well as a weathered finish to reflect how the helmet appears in-game.
Two AAA batteries power LED lighting, which can be swapped between Paragon Blue and Renegade Red using an internal switch. No neutral options here.
The helmet is now up for preorder for $174.99, with no indiciation of a release date. Whenever it does ship, that price gets you the wearable helmet as well as a weighted stand, plaque, and challenge coin.
The official Bioware merch drop includes two more 'new' releases: a pair of Converse-like N7 sneakers, and a new T-shirt dedicated to a particularly beloved companion, Garrus Vakarian. Otherwise, the Official Bioware Store has dropped discounts on a range of existing N7 merch, including hats, sweaters, and statues.
The actual products come from DPI Merchandise, a company that has long partnered with Bioware alongside fellow RPG giants like Bethesda and CD Projekt Red.
As for what else fans can expect this weekend? A rumored Mass Effect 5 trailer began circulating around social media platforms soon after news hit of the studio's closure. It's possible Bioware was planning to debut said trailer on N7 Day, but that ship has now sailed.
While a "Save Mess Effect" petition has picked up over 300,000 signatures, for now, fans will have to make do with the merch.
Reports have continued to trickle out about what exactly led to the studio’s closure. Saudi Arabi's PIF, Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners completed their acquisition of EA this past August in a deal valued at $55 billion. The company was quick to announce a new strategy focused on "core titles" and increased investment in AI development.
One report suggests EA’s new strategy led the company to a choice between Star Wars: Battlefront 3 and Mass Effect 5, and the company went with the former. A newly announced documentary will hopefully answer questions about what exactly went down in Bioware’s final years, while paying tribute to a studio that defined the modern RPG.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Dead by Daylight has returned to 'Mostly Positive' recent reviews on Steam after Valve labeled a chunk of ratings surrounding TheBurntPeanut backlash as 'off-topic.'
item.description:
Dead by Daylight has returned to 'Mostly Positive' recent reviews on Steam after Valve labeled a chunk of ratings surrounding TheBurntPeanut backlash as 'off-topic.'
To catch you up to speed, developer Behaviour Interactive's recent work with controversial streamer TheBurntPeanut landed its asymmetrical horror game in the line of fire. A few apologetic posts and hundreds of comments later, Dead by Daylight spent much of this week showing declining favorability ratings on Steam (via SteamDB) – but that now seems to be a thing of the past.
Check out its Steam page today, and you'll find that Dead by Daylight now boasts 'Mostly Positive' reviews, with a little asterisk clarifying the reasoning for this sudden jump. A disclaimer shared in the reviews section of its page notes that the dates between November 1 – 6 have been noted for off-topic activity. Valve explained that the range has been "marked as containing an abnormal set of reviews that we believe are largely unrelated to the likelihood that you would enjoy the product." As a result, "the reviews within this period are excluded from the Review Score by default."
Dead by Daylight 10th Anniversary Broadcast Visual Overhaul Reveal - Screenshots
Steam users have the freedom to unmark the reviews Steam has deemed to be off-topic. Doing so reflects a 'Mixed' score instead, with the Mostly Positive rating shown by default. After a week of back-and-forth between Behaviour and its community, fans generally have been unhappy with Dead by Daylight, even if the reaction comes from behavior outside of the game itself. Although reviews may seem to be back on track, fans across social media still want to make their voices heard.
"They can't reverse the damage to their reputation or s***ty customer service," one player said.
"In this case, Valve is wrong," another argued. "The negative reviews were completely justified."
Meanwhile, there has been some confusion from the Dead by Daylight community regarding what Valve's process is for labeling reviews as off-topic. It's something the company directly addressed in a 2019 blog post, with it, at the time, saying its goal was to remove anomalous activity that could inaccurately reflect a game's rating based on factors the average player doesn't care about.
It's Valve's attempt to combat review-bombing campaigns that it's incorporated for years, with it saying that it had developed a tool "that identifies any anomalous review activity on all games on Steam in as close to real-time as possible." Its description continued: "It doesn't know why a given game is receiving anomalous review activity, and it doesn't even try to figure that out. Instead, it notifies a team of people at Valve, who'll then go and investigate."
If investigators believe activity within a certain period fits the definition of off-topic, Valve will "mark the time period it encompasses and notify the developer." How the Steam company's process for identifying and neutralizing inauthentic reviews may have changed in the last seven and a half years is unclear.
When reached for clarification, Behaviour told IGN it "is not at liberty to discuss any platform partner (review) processes" and pointed to its most recent statement related to this week's controversy. IGN has also reached out to Valve for comment and clarification.
As Dead by Daylight returns to general positivity on Steam, the period of controversy does seem to have come to an end. Behaviour's most recent public comment on the matter saw it clarify that it had removed gifted content from TheBurntPeanut's account, while promising that it would be "taking appropriate action" regarding how the incident happened in the first place.
Dead By Daylight's New Urban Map for All-Kill: Comeback
Last month, the studio announced Child's Play Killer Chucky would be the latest icon removed from sale. It told IGN in a statement that Killers will "continue to have an open invitation to join (or rejoin)."
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: It was announced less than a year ago, but Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble — a mobile spin-off of the flagship PlayStation series — has been canceled.
item.description:
It was announced less than a year ago, but Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble — a mobile spin-off of the flagship PlayStation series — has been canceled. Today marks the final update to the game, and it will shut down entirely in May 2027. The game was technically still in a soft launch phase, ahead of a full global release.
"We’ve made the difficult decision to cease development of Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble. The final planned update will be rolling out November 6th, 2026, and the app will be removed from stores on November 21st, 2026. Players who already have the game will be able to continue playing until May 1st, 2027, when the game’s servers will permanently shut down. On behalf of the dev team and everyone helping to make the game, thanks to our amazing community for all your support, especially to those who have spent time playing, sharing feedback, and helping shape Ranger Rumble throughout its development!"
According to the official announcement, in-app purchases have been removed from the game, with the announcement advising players to use any in-game rewards or currency before the game shuts down. In an FAQ, players seeking some sort of refund for money spent are directed to Apple’s App Store or Google Play customer support.
The game offered arena shooter-style action with characters from the series and was developed by Oh BiBi in collaboration with Insonmiac Games and PlayStation Studios. As recently as July, the PlayStation blog shared that the game was "gearing up for global launch" after "a successful testing phase shaped by player feedback."
Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

item.title: Sony has announced a range of new “perks” for PS Plus, including a three-month trial to YouTube Premium, as well as trials and discounts for other services. But not all fans are on board.
item.description:
Sony has announced a range of new “perks” for PS Plus, including a three-month trial to YouTube Premium, as well as trials and discounts for other services. But not all fans are on board.
"Enjoy a range of special offers, trials and discounts from PlayStation, Sony and select partners. All included with your PlayStation Plus membership," Sony's announcement reads.
Those partners include YouTube Premium, DAZN, Audible, and Sony Pictures' own Core. Elsewhere, PS Plus members get a 5% discount when they buy direct from PlayStation, they can save 10% on gaming and audio from Sony Electronics, and a two month trial of Calm Premium.
The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time
"How is a free trial a perk?" one person complained on social media. "Calling free trials a perk is a big reach," another person commented. "These are not real perks, these are just money for Sony by funnelling people into these other subscriptions," another said. "Nobody cares about a free trial. Give us full crunchy roll premium on ps plus and then maybe we will be happy," one person suggested.
Others are using the perks announcement to once again criticize Sony for its decision to kill PlayStation discs from 2028. “Are Physical discs a perk?” said one social media user. “This reeks of desperation,” said another before continuing: “So many people have abandoned PS Plus as a result of Sony’s plans to end physical discs, that they are now trying to entice people with the old carrot and the stick routine.”
The disc backlash does not appear to have affected Sony's bottom line so far. In Sony’s recent financial results, the number of monthly active users (MAUs) across the PlayStation platform actually increased 7% in September compared to the same month of the previous fiscal year to 127 million accounts — that’s a record high for September. Sony said this indicates “the baseline of engagement is steadily improving.”
According to the same results, 78% of game sales over the period were digital, which is a significant majority. With digital sales of first-party games, Sony gets the full cut of revenue.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel is probably still a couple years away, and we don't know much about Bethesda's next big MMO. However, the game director for Skyrim has come out with a couple of specific requests for the game.
item.description:
The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel is probably still a couple years away, and we don't know much about Bethesda's next big RPG. However, the game director for Skyrim has come out with a couple of specific requests for the game.
Former Bethesda design director Bruce Nesmith sat down on The Examined Game podcast to talk about his time at the company. But, about 40 minutes into the interview, the YouTuber asked Nesmith about what he'd like to see from The Elder Scrolls VI, and there are two things, better mounts and better ladders. And that latter one is how you can tell that he's a game director.
Wanting better mounts in Elder Scrolls is almost universal for fans, as Skyrim doesn't exactly have a great mount system. As Nesmith describes the problem, "you can ride a horse, but that's all you can do in Skyrim. Thats it. You just ride the horse. Well, I should be able to do other things with the horse, too, like maybe fight on the horse, or have it fight with me, or you know, stuff like that."
Every IGN Elder Scrolls Review
To be clear, Nesmith now spends his days writing novels, and doesn't have anything to do with Sentinel, but it would be cool to be able to have some kind of mounted combat system in The Elder Scrolls VI. For instance, I've been getting back into Monster Hunter Wilds ahead of the expansion, and the way you can use your Seikret to dodge out of boss mechanics and manage your inventory while avoiding attacks is huge, and would be great in other RPGs.
But as for ladders, Nesmith request seems odd until he starts to explain the way that ladders limited game design in Skyrim. As he explains, "you don't climb up and down ladders. It seems simple, it seems stupid, but you don't climb up and down ladders, which really limits the art team in terms of how they can do multi-layer things. You know, all the ladders in Skyrim, you click on the ladder, and poof you're at the top. Or you have to climb a stair."
Some of that is obviously the limited technology of 2011, but it's apparently something Bethesda tried to solve, before giving up to prioritize other elements of the massive RPG. When Nesmith tried to get ladders solved in Skyrim, he says "to do ladders, you have to deal with a whole host of questions that our programmers very legitimately put in front of us and said, 'you give me answers to these, I'll tell you how much programming time it's going to take to make them.' and that caused problems right there."
Even when I sit down and think about it, I can't really think of any game that really nails ladders, and a lot of games have problems with them in one way or another, especially around the era of Skyrim. Nesmith goes on to explain a lot of the specific problems that enemy AI has with ladders, like its ability to decide whether or not to wait for you at the top, or to climb back down the ladder to come after you. These problems have all been solved in one way or another in other games, but I'd hope that Skyrim finds a way to solve the issue as well.
Either way, The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel is still a few years away, even though Bethesda is already selling merch. We'll have to wait a bit to see more about the game, but there are some signs about what might be in the game, and that might even include ship combat – or at least I hope.
What kind of world do you hope The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel will provide?

item.title: Adam Driver, best known for his turn as Kylo Ren in the Star Wars sequel trilogy, has discussed finally joining the MCU as X-Men villain Mister Sinister.
item.description:
Adam Driver, best known for his turn as Kylo Ren in the Star Wars sequel trilogy, is finally going to be a part of the MCU after years of speculation. But instead of playing Magneto as rumors suggested, he landed the role of Mister Sinister in the upcoming X-Men reboot.
During a recent Jimmy Kimmel segment, Driver spoke briefly about the role and what drew him to it. “I was a big X-Men fan when I was a kid,” Driver said. “The TV show was right in my generation. It’s huge for me. Me and my cousin, Tony, he would be Sabretooth and I would be Wolverine — it’s a big deal.”
In the comics, Mister Sinister is the persona of Dr. Nathaniel Essex, a London biologist obsessed with engineering humanity into a perfect race of superhumans. When Kimmel mentioned the name of the supervillain on the segment, Driver couldn’t help but smile.
MCU X-Men Cast as of D23 2026
It’s a character he’s clearly excited about playing. As Kimmel pointed out on the show, Driver has been offered multiple roles by president of Marvel Studios Kevin Feige, but he’s turned them all down. He’s never wanted to be a part of the MCU, until now.
“I was a fan of the other things too, but this one felt like the right time, and it’s X-Men,” Driver said. Driver credited part of his willingness to take the role on working with director Jake Schreier, best known for the brilliant Netflix show Beef, and Marvel’s Thunderbolts.
“[Schreier's] idea for it, and Kevin Feige, it all came together, the script is really cool,” he said.
Wrapping things up, Kimmel asked why Driver is so careful when he says yes to a project. “A lot of people are going to watch it, and if it’s bad, people will see you being bad,” Driver replied. “Plus, I don’t want to mess it up. I’m a huge fan of X-Men.”
So far, Marvel Studios has confirmed a long list of names for its new MCU X-Men movie reboot, with its cast now including Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops, and more.
Photo by Matei Horvath/FilmMagic.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Actor Blythe Melin is now the voice of the male protagonist and his brother, J, in The Expanse: Osiris Reborn. This comes after fan reaction to the beta, which accused the voice work of being “flat” and “boring.”
item.description:
Actor Blythe Melin is now the voice of the male protagonist and his brother, J, in The Expanse: Osiris Reborn. This comes after fan reaction to the beta, which accused the voice work of being “flat” and “boring.”
"While the voice actor for the male protagonist and J put in a lot of good work, they felt less expressive than we wanted," said the developer in a blog post earlier this year, before a replacement was announced. "Because of this, we are changing the voices of the male protagonist and J."
Melin is best known for his roles in animation, particularly in the DC comics universe, but the U.S.-based actor has also worked in video games doing mostly background NPC voices. As far as I can tell, developer Owlcat never announced who the previous actor was.
The Expanse: Osiris Reborn Updated Male Protagonist Face Screenshots
Funnily enough, this isn’t the only game inspired by Mass Effect to change the look of its protagonist based on fan feedback. Upcoming sci-fi RPG Exodus also did a redesign of its male protagonist the other week.
For me, The Expanse: Osiris Reborn's new protagonist looks like Marco Inaros, the terrorist leader and commander of the Free Navy in The Expanse TV show. He liked flinging asteroids at Earth but was pretty chill about it. Anyway, the new face looks a lot like him — maybe it’s the hair in the example images.
That hair is up to you, of course. You’re able to customize how your protagonist looks, whether you choose the male or female version of the character. But like Commander Shepard has a canon look, so will this pair. Details on who voices the female protagonist and other cast members are coming at a later date.
"Voicing both the Captain and J has been an incredible joy and a unique challenge compared to the rest of my work voicing in video games over the years,” Blythe Melin said. “TWO, biologically related characters! It presented a difficult task in itself, because I find it very important to make sure neither character felt one-note-ey or too similar to the other.
“The more a character talks, especially in a multi-path dialogue route like for this game, the harder the task of making characters feel fleshed out while still having their own flavors and mannerisms. Playing twins has definitely been tricky, but there is somewhat of an easy divide that can be made between the Captain and J, in that one is an avatar for the player themselves, and the other is a pre-established co-character within the context of The Expanse. This allowed us to give J more of a solidified personality to work off of, with a lot of credit going to the writers and directors."
The Expanse: Osiris Reborn launches on PC, Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5 in spring 2027.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Developer KAFI has announced its next game, titled Snow Panic, which is an eight-player arcadey online skiing game that one of its developers describes as being like "SSX meets Mario Kart." It's in development for PC.
item.description:
Developer KAFI has announced its next game, titled Snow Panic, which is an eight-player arcadey online skiing game that one of its developers describes as being like "SSX meets Mario Kart." It's in development for PC.
It's a downhill skiing game that will always feature competition; bots will fill in if you don't have enough human players in the match. And in that downhill race, the only rule is that the first one to reach the bottom wins. Bullets, rockets, and "suspiciously aggressive wildlife" will be amongst the obstacles you have to overcome as you ski towards the bottom. The developers mention airstrikes, mines, and a literal exploding goat as other hazards. Check out the announcement trailer below.
A clean run sounds like it's virtually impossible, by design. "Every hit is a full ragdoll crash, and every crash is somebody’s favorite clip," KAFI said. Expect six mountains to race on at launch, with more promised in post-release updates. Snow Panic also features proximity voice chat, because, as the team notes, "What’s the point of blowing up your friends if you can’t hear them scream as they fall into a ravine?"
There are 14 total weapons and items available at launch, and you'll be able to customize your skier's hair, outfits, and skis. You can wishlist Snow Panic on Steam if you're interested.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: The live-action Stranger Things prequel series has its first teaser trailer and a 2028 release window, Netflix has announced.
item.description:
The live-action Stranger Things prequel series has its first teaser trailer and a 2028 release window, Netflix has announced.
“Before Hawkins, there was Marion,” reads the tagline. The show is called Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure, and it’s from The Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry.
Before Hawkins, there was Marion.Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure. A new series only on Netflix. 2028. https://t.co/NvISItwYAF
The series is a prequel set in the 1950s, before Stranger Things and before the stage play Stranger Things: The First Shadow, which explores Henry Creel’s troubled past in Hawkins in 1959. Specifically, the teaser confirms April 19, 1955, in Marion, Nevada. We see a discarded bike outside a fenced off restricted area. "Use of deadly force authorized," reads the warning sign. The camera pans up to reveal a mystery facility lit up at night, before we move to focus on the sky above. Then there's a blink and you'll miss it look at what seems to be a UFO.
Golden Globe-winning director Joe Wright is set to direct the first three episodes of the new series, with production to take place in New Mexico. Expect a new era, setting and all-new characters, themes and mythology, Netflix added.
Jinny Howe, Netflix Head of Scripted Series, US & Canada: “Stranger Things has always belonged to the fans, and their passion made it a worldwide phenomenon. Today, on Stranger Things Day, we’re honored to partner again with Matt and Ross Duffer and Kate Trefry to give fans a new dimension of this universe to step into. Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure takes us to the 1950s with new heroes and all the heart, mystery, and spectacle of the original series. We’re proud to keep building this world with the Duffers, Kate, Shawn Levy, and Joe Wright, and we can’t wait for fans to see what’s next.”

Co-Creators/Executive Producers Matt & Ross Duffer commented: “We’ve been dreaming of Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure for many years now, and to see it become a reality is surreal and exhilarating. We’re so grateful to our incredible team of collaborators: our showrunner Kate Trefry, who has been in the trenches with us since Season 2 and wrote Stranger Things: The First Shadow; and our director, Joe Wright, a brilliant artist whose work we’ve long admired. We can’t wait for you to see what they’re cooking up. It’s Stranger Things, but also thrillingly fresh, with a new setting, new heroes and villains, and new… actually, we’re not allowed to say any more. Now, on to casting. In the meantime -- watch the skies, nerds!”
Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure is far from the first Stranger Things spinoff we've seen from Netflix since the hit show came to an end in January, but it does promise to answer some burning questions left by the end of Season 5.
Warning! Spoilers for Stranger Things Season 5 Episode 8, The Rightside Up, follow:
In the Season 5 finale, we see Henry Creel / Vecna finally face his greatest fear: the traumatic memory of the day he was infected by the Mind Flayer and gained his powers. In this scene set inside Henry’s mind, we finally find out what was inside the briefcase that child Henry opens after bludgeoning its previous owner, an unnamed scientist, to death. Inside is a mysterious rock, which glows with an unknown energy before fusing with Henry. This, we understand, is how Henry became one with the Mind Flayer, and sets in motion all the events of Stranger Things that followed.
But what was this rock exactly, and how did it come to be in our world in the first place? An article on Netflix published as Stranger Things came to an end confirms the rock contains Mind Flayer particles, which then possess Henry. “Come find me,” the Mind Flayer beckons. And the dying scientist warns: “It will consume you.”
In a subsequent interview with Variety, Stranger Things co-creators Matt and Ross Duffer teased that the planned spinoff, which we now know to be Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure, will explain all — and answer other plot threads left dangling.
“The spinoff is going to delve into that and explain that, and you’re going to understand it,” Matt Duffer said of the briefcase rock. “But it’s a completely different mythology. So it’s not a deep exploration of the Mind Flayer or anything like that. It’s very fresh and very new, but yes, it will answer some of the loose threads that are remaining.”

The briefcase scene is explained in vague terms by Stranger Things: The First Shadow, the canon play that acts as a prequel to the events of the Netflix show. We've run through the plot of the play already, but in summary, it confirms that Henry and the scientist are transported to what was then known as Dimension X. When Henry returns, he is much changed, and Dr. Brenner (Matthew Modine) eventually uses him as part of his experiments in Hawkins National Laboratory.
But even before then, the play tells us of a 1943 United States experiment to turn submarines invisible during World War 2. As part of this, they travel to Dimension X. Perhaps that's where the mysterious rock originally came from, and how it ended up in our world in the first place.
The Duffers previously described the spinoff as a “clean slate.” “Completely new characters, new town, new world, new mythology,” Matt Duffer said, adding: “No common characters.”
